question: On 15 December 2023, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control urged the EU Member States to strengthen vaccination campaigns and prepare for the possible need to increase emergency department and ICU capacity, as well as to consider a number of public health measures to reduce the impact of respiratory pathogens circulating this winter. Among other things, it recommended the use of face masks.

In Spain, the ‘tripledemic’, a combination of flu, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus, is giving rise to growing concern in healthcare facilities and filling up emergency departments. Twenty-four days after the EU alert and recommendations were published, the Spanish Government brought together the autonomous communities to put in place appropriate measures. 1.

Does the Commission believe that Member States should ensure greater prevention and preparedness, in line with EU recommendations, and does it intend to expand the recommendations and measures in the face of a possible increase in cases, not just in Spain but across the EU?

Does it support the need for coordination among administrations to harmonise criteria in advance with a view to preventing a rise in infections and ensuring that healthcare facilities are better prepared?
answer: The Commission, with the implementation of Regulation 2022/2371 on serious cross-border threats to healt h (1), and Regulation 2022/2370 on the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) enhanced mandat e (2), is contributing to better preparedness and response planning at EU and Member State level.
At EU level, coordination on prevention, preparedness and response takes place in the Health Security Committee (HSC), which can issue opinions and guidance, including on specific response measures.

The Commission is following the evolution of the epidemiological situation around respiratory viruses in regular meetings of the HSC, with the support of the ECDC, as during autumn/winter 2023/2024 in which there have been high rates of respiratory infections. There have been several HSC general working group meetings where the topic has been discussed, including the HSC senior level group.

(3) On 19 October 2023, the HSC issued an Opinion on preparing for winter 2023/2024 to address respiratory infections caused by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and other viruses, such as influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (4). This opinion proposes certain prevention, preparedness and response measures to Member States.

In full respect with the competences conferred to it by the Treaties, Union action respects the Member States’ responsibilities for the definition of their national health policies and for the organisation and delivery of health services.
